children: White sugar futures on ICE edged up on Monday amid further signs of shrinking supplies in Europe, the world's third-largest producer after Brazil and India.
There was no trading in raw sugar, arabica coffee and New York cocoa futures due to the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
SUGAR
* White sugar
settled up 0.6% at $526 a metric ton.

* Germany's 2026/27 refined sugar production is forecast to fall 23.4% versus the prior season to 3.386 million tons, after a sharp cut in the beet sowing area and a severe summer drought and heatwave.
* The El Nino weather pattern continues to pose a significant threat to sugar output in key growers India and Thailand.
* El Niño is set to intensify further into 2027 and could be the strongest ever, raising risks of extreme weather into next year, the World Meteorological Organization said.
* Pakistan issued a tender to sell and export 107,739 metric tons of white refined sugar.
* Raw sugar
closed little changed on Friday at 18.07 cents per lb, having hit a 16-month peak earlier that week.
COFFEE
* Robusta coffee
settled down 0.7% to $3,405 a ton, after hitting a 2-1/2-month low last week.
* Uganda's coffee exports declined 15.1% in July from a year ago. The East African country is the world's third-largest robusta grower.
* Coffee is under pressure overall though from an expected bumper 2026/27 crop in top grower Brazil.
* Brazil exported 45% more coffee in August than in the same month a year before.
* Arabica coffee
closed little changed on Friday at $2.956 per lb, having hit a five-week low earlier that week.
COCOA
* London cocoa
settled little changed at £4,519 per ton, some way off last Tuesday's one-year high of £4,988.
* El Nino is a worry for cocoa. But those concerns have lessened somewhat as, so far, the weather pattern has not brought excess rains to West Africa.
* New York cocoa
closed up 0.2% at $6,188 a ton on Friday.
